metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (VB6 form with ADODB database connection, Form_Load entry point) present with a dependency on Microsoft Access database. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: The application performs write operations (INSERT INTO Customers) against a persistent database (Microsoft Access .mdb). It owns data via CRUD operations. Classified as stateful-crud.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Overall score 1.05 yields the Not Ready band (< 1.5) but 11 High findings yield Remediation Required tier (2-11 High range). The divergence occurs because the system scores uniformly at 1 across nearly all questions but only 14 of 37 questions are designated as core (producing High findings at score 1). The remaining non-core questions at score 1 produce Medium findings. The score-based signal is the stronger indicator: this system is fundamentally not ready for cloud-native operation.

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: All compute is a Win32 desktop EXE (VB6 runtime) running on field sales laptops. No cloud compute of any kind.
findings.gap: No managed compute. The application runs entirely on end-user desktops with no centralized compute, no elasticity, and no operational control.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite as a web application deployed on ECS Fargate or Lambda.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: Primary database is Microsoft Access 2003 (.mdb) on an SMB file share. Reporting database is SQL Server 2012 synced via DTS/SSIS. Both are self-managed.
findings.gap: All databases are self-managed with no automated failover, no managed backups, and monthly corruption.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL as part of the application rewrite.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: No workflow orchestration service in use. The nightly DTS/SSIS sync is a scheduled batch job with no managed orchestration.
findings.gap: The DTS/SSIS nightly sync is a legacy, unmanaged workflow with no error handling, no retry logic, and no execution visibility.
findings.recommendation: Use AWS Step Functions or EventBridge Scheduler for orchestration in the rewritten system.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. All data access is synchronous. Data movement is via nightly DTS/SSIS batch only.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross service boundaries. Customer record creation is not propagated in real-time.
findings.recommendation: Use SQS or EventBridge to emit events on customer record changes in the rewritten application.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: No network security controls. Desktop app connects directly to SMB file share with embedded credentials. No VPC, no segmentation.
findings.gap: No network isolation. Database access is over SMB with no segmentation between client and data tier.
findings.recommendation: Deploy the database in a private subnet with security groups restricting access to the application service only.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: No API entry point. Desktop app connects directly to database with no gateway, load balancer, or API layer.
findings.gap: Direct database exposure from client devices with no API gateway, no throttling, no request validation.
findings.recommendation: Expose a REST API via API Gateway with authentication, throttling, and request validation.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling. Desktop app with static Access database on a single file server. Capacity is fixed.
findings.gap: No elasticity. The Access database corrupts under concurrent writes (~monthly).
findings.recommendation: Configure auto-scaling on compute and data layers in the rewritten architecture.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration. Access .mdb on single file server with no failover. Monthly corruption with no recovery capability.
findings.gap: No backup or recovery capability. A file server failure could result in complete data loss.
findings.recommendation: Use managed database services with automated backups (Aurora with PITR, DynamoDB continuous backups).

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: Zero IaC coverage. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or any IaC. All infrastructure manually provisioned.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. All infrastructure created and maintained manually with no reproducibility.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in Terraform or CDK as part of the rewrite.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD automation. README states: 'No tests, no build server; compiled on one developer's machine.' Deployment is manual EXE copy.
findings.gap: Zero automation. Build is manual, deployment is manual, no testing at any stage.
findings.recommendation: Establish a CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions or AWS CodePipeline) with build, test, and deploy stages.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Application written in Visual Basic 6.0 (released 1998, unsupported). No AWS SDK, no cloud-native tooling, no modern framework ecosystem.
findings.gap: VB6 has no AWS SDK and no cloud-native tooling. Language itself must be replaced before any modernization.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in Python (FastAPI), TypeScript (NestJS), or Java/Kotlin (Spring Boot) depending on team skills.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: Tightly-coupled monolith. Single VB6 form contains UI, business logic, data access, and configuration with no separation of concerns.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith with pervasive shared state. No module boundaries, no abstraction layers.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite using Hexagonal Architecture with clear separation of API, domain, and data access layers.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: All communication is synchronous ADO calls. No async patterns. State changes not propagated to downstream systems in real-time.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous with no async patterns. Customer changes propagated only via nightly batch.
findings.recommendation: Emit domain events on state changes via SQS or EventBridge in the rewritten service.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. Errors swallowed with On Error Resume Next. No async job processing.
findings.gap: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. No background processing capability.
findings.recommendation: Implement async patterns for operations exceeding 30 seconds using SQS workers or Step Functions.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No API exists. Desktop app connecting directly to database with no API surface to version.
findings.gap: No API and no versioning strategy.
findings.recommendation: Design new API with URL-path versioning (e.g., /v1/customers) from day one.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: All endpoints hardcoded. Database path is a constant (S:\CRM\sales.mdb). No service registry or dynamic configuration.
findings.gap: Hardcoded service endpoints. Any change requires recompilation and redistribution.
findings.recommendation: Use environment variables or AWS Service Discovery for dynamic endpoint configuration.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: Data stored on local file system — Access .mdb on SMB share. Proprietary format, single file server, monthly corruption.
findings.gap: Data on legacy local file system with no managed storage, no accessibility, and regular corruption.
findings.recommendation: Migrate customer data to managed database (Aurora/RDS). Store unstructured documents in S3.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Database access scattered in UI form code. SQL constructed via string concatenation in event handlers. No repository/DAO pattern.
findings.gap: Database queries in UI code with no data access abstraction. SQL injection vulnerability present.
findings.recommendation: Implement repository/DAO pattern with parameterized queries in the rewritten service.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: Both database engines past EOL. Microsoft Access 2003/Jet OLEDB 4.0 is EOL for over a decade. SQL Server 2012 reached end of extended support July 2022.
findings.gap: All database engines past EOL. No security patches, known vulnerabilities unaddressed, no upgrade path.
findings.recommendation: Replace with current managed services: Aurora PostgreSQL (current version) for primary workload.

findings.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
findings.description: No stored procedures in application code. However, relies on proprietary constructs: Jet OLEDB 4.0, Jet SQL dialect (Now()), DTS/SSIS for data sync.
findings.gap: Moderate reliance on proprietary SQL constructs creating migration barriers (Jet OLEDB, Jet SQL, DTS/SSIS).
findings.recommendation: Use standard SQL (PostgreSQL-compatible) and replace DTS/SSIS with AWS Glue or EventBridge-driven sync.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest. Access .mdb on SMB share with only a trivially bypassable database password. Customer data in plaintext.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest for customer data. The .mdb password is not encryption.
findings.recommendation: Use managed database services with encryption at rest enabled and customer-managed KMS keys.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: No API authentication. Database access uses hardcoded password. No application-level auth beyond Windows network login.
findings.gap: No API authentication. Anyone with file share access or source code can access all customer data.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT authentication via Amazon Cognito in the rewritten service.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: No identity integration. Application uses Windows USERNAME environment variable as identity proxy and hardcoded DB password.
findings.gap: No identity provider integration. No application-level authentication.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito or corporate IdP via SAML/OIDC federation.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: Plaintext credentials hardcoded in source: Private Const DB_PW As String = "crm2005pw". Visible in repo and git history.
findings.gap: Hardcoded plaintext database password in source code. Critical security vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Store all credentials in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation. Rotate the current password immediately.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No compute hardening or patching strategy. App runs on unmanaged field laptops with VB6 compat shim. No vulnerability scanning.
findings.gap: No patching strategy, no vulnerability scanning, no compute hardening.
findings.recommendation: Use managed compute (Fargate, Lambda) in the rewritten architecture to eliminate OS patching responsibility.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools. No CI/CD pipeline exists. Known SQL injection vulnerability in source undetected by any tool.
findings.gap: No security scanning. Known vulnerabilities exist undetected.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST, dependency scanning, and container scanning into the CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No OpenTelemetry, no X-Ray. Errors swallowed with On Error Resume Next.
findings.gap: No observability. Operations are invisible — errors swallowed with no logging or tracing.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with OpenTelemetry or X-Ray SDK from day one in the rewritten service.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No monitoring. Monthly corruption and record-locked errors suggest implicit SLOs are regularly violated.
findings.gap: No SLO definitions or monitoring of any kind.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for availability, latency, and error rate in the rewritten service.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business or infrastructure metrics. Only implicit metric is monthly corruption count.
findings.gap: No metrics of any kind — neither business nor infrastructure.
findings.recommendation: Publish business metrics (customers created, active users) via CloudWatch custom metrics.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. Failures discovered only when users encounter error message boxes.
findings.gap: No alerting. No proactive detection of failures.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch anomaly detection on error rates and latency with PagerDuty integration.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: No automated tests. README states: 'No tests, no build server.' Zero test coverage since 2005.
findings.gap: Zero test coverage. No safety net for changes.
findings.recommendation: Establish integration tests for all critical workflows running in CI pipeline.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No dashboards, no alarms, no CODEOWNERS, no monitoring of any kind.
findings.gap: No observability infrastructure and no ownership model.
findings.recommendation: Establish per-service dashboards and alarms with named team ownership.
